lesson_title: Writing IAM Policies — Precision Permissions with Conditions
student_will_learn: How to write multi-statement IAM policies from scratch
The exact difference between bucket-level and object-level S3 ARNs
How to use Condition keys to restrict access by IP, time, or tags
How to design a policy that grants broad read but narrow write access
How to identify and fix the most common IAM policy mistakes

ava_lesson_intro.ava_speaks: கடைசி 2 lessons-ல policy structure தெரிஞ்சுக்கிட்டீங்க, role attach பண்ணீங்க. இன்னைக்கு அடுத்த level-க்கு போவோம் — complex real-world policies எழுதப் போறோம். Multiple statements, conditions, precise resource scoping. இது தான் senior cloud engineer-ங்க daily work பண்ற level.

lines: Building Basics · Session CS2 · Lesson C2.2

blocks.block_title: Resource ARNs — Bucket vs Object Level
blocks.ava_speaks: S3-ல ரெண்டு மாதிரி ARN இருக்கு, இது தான் ரொம்ப பேரு confuse ஆகுற இடம். arn:aws:s3:::my-bucket — இது bucket itself. arn:aws:s3:::my-bucket/* — இது bucket-க்குள்ள இருக்க objects. Bucket-level operations — s3:ListBucket மாதிரி — bucket ARN வேணும், /* இல்லாம. Object-level operations — s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject மாதிரி — object ARN வேணும், /*-உடன். இது ரெண்டையும் confuse பண்ணா, ஒரு classic bug வரும் — ListBucket permission கொடுத்தாலும், 'Access Denied' வரும், ஏன்னா wrong ARN format use பண்ணி இருப்பீங்க. இப்போ Condition keys பாப்போம். Condition-ன்னா, policy-க்கு ஒரு extra rule add பண்றது. 'இந்த access-ஐ, இந்த IP range-ல இருந்து வந்தா மட்டும் allow பண்ணு' மாதிரி. aws:SourceIp, aws:RequestedRegion, s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption — இதெல்லாம் common condition keys.

board_actions.text: S3 ARN — Two Levels, Two Different Rules

rows: Requires BOTH ARN formats in the policy

board_actions.text: Classic mistake: giving ListBucket permission on the object ARN (with /*) instead of the bucket ARN. Result: 'Access Denied' even though the permission looks correct.

Condition: An optional extra rule in a policy statement that must ALSO be true for the Allow/Deny to apply. Example: only allow if aws:SourceIp is within the office IP range. Conditions can also check TIME — DateGreaterThan / DateLessThan on aws:CurrentTime restricts an action to a window (e.g. business hours only), and tag checks like ec2:ResourceTag/Owner restrict by ownership.

inline_questions.question: What does 'arn:aws:s3:::photos-bucket/*' in a Resource field specifically cover?
options: A) The photos-bucket bucket and all objects inside it
B) Only the objects inside photos-bucket, not the bucket itself
C) All S3 buckets that start with 'photos'
D) The bucket, its objects, and any sub-buckets
inline_questions.ava_correct: Correct! /* means objects INSIDE the bucket only. Bucket itself-க்கு ஆனா separate ARN வேணும், without the /*.
inline_questions.ava_wrong: இல்ல. photos-bucket/* — இந்த /* object-level-ஐ மட்டும் refer பண்ணும். Bucket itself list பண்ண வேணும்னா, /* இல்லாம வேற ARN வேணும்.

inline_questions.question: A user has Policy A (Allow s3:DeleteObject on *) and Policy B (Deny s3:DeleteObject on arn:aws:s3:::production-bucket/*). The user tries to delete a file in 'production-bucket'. What happens?
options: A) Allow wins — Policy A was attached first
B) Deny wins — explicit Deny in Policy B overrides Allow in Policy A
C) Delete succeeds because Policy A explicitly allows it
D) AWS asks the user to confirm which policy applies
inline_questions.ava_correct: சரி! Deny always wins. Production bucket-ல delete = denied. Test bucket-ல delete = allowed (no Deny அங்க). இது production protection pattern.
inline_questions.ava_wrong: இல்ல, remember — Deny explicit-ஆ இருந்தா, அது எப்போவுமே win பண்ணும். Policy A-ல Allow இருந்தாலும், Policy B-ன் Deny அதை override பண்ணும்.

blocks.ava_speaks: Razorpay-ல payment receipts S3-ல store ஆகும். இது ரொம்ப sensitive data. அவங்க bucket policy எப்படி design பண்ணி இருக்காங்கன்னா — ஒரே ஒரு specific Lambda function ARN மட்டும் அந்த bucket-ஐ read பண்ண முடியும். Senior developers கூட directly access பண்ண முடியாது. Condition key use பண்ணி, Principal-ஐ அந்த specific Lambda ARN-க்கு மட்டும் restrict பண்ணி இருக்காங்க. இது compliance requirement-க்காக — payment data யாரு access பண்றாங்கன்னு exact-ஆ control பண்ணணும். இது தான் precision permission design.

board_actions.text: Razorpay: Bucket Policy Restricting to One Lambda ARN

rows: Any IAM user with S3 permissions

blocks.ava_speaks: இப்போ real policy எழுதப் போறோம் — FoodQuick-ன் data team-க்காக. Read all buckets, write ஒரே ஒரு specific bucket-க்கு மட்டும்.

steps.ava_narration: முதல் statement — read access, all buckets-க்கும். Action list பண்றோம், Resource-க்கு * கொடுக்கறோம்.
இரண்டாவது statement — write access, ஒரே ஒரு bucket-க்கு மட்டும் — foodquick-analytics.
கடைசியா, ஒரு Condition add பண்றோம் — office IP range-லிருந்து மட்டும் இந்த write access வேலை செய்யும்.

expected_outcome.description: A complete 2-statement policy: broad read access everywhere, narrow write access to one bucket, restricted further by office IP condition
expected_outcome.what_to_notice: Two separate statements handle two separate permission levels. This is cleaner than trying to combine read and write logic into one statement.

blocks.ava_speaks: இந்த policy-ஐ, ஒரு data analyst use பண்ணும்போது என்ன நடக்கும்-ன்னு பாருங்க.

ascii: Request: PutObject on 'foodquick-analytics' from office IP
Request: PutObject on 'foodquick-analytics' from home WiFi
→ Matches Statement 2 BUT Condition fails → DENIED

output_preview.ava_narration: Same person, same bucket, ஆனா location மாறினா result மாறும். Condition key-ன் power இது தான்.

blocks.block_title: Your Turn — Write the ML Team Policy
blocks.instruction: FoodQuick's ML team needs a precisely scoped policy. Write the complete JSON.
blocks.scenario: The ML team needs: read access to ALL S3 buckets (they analyze data from many sources), write access ONLY to 'foodquick-ml-training-data' bucket, and the ability to create/terminate ONLY their own EC2 instances (identified by an 'Owner' tag matching their username) — never touching instances owned by other teams.
requirements: Statement 1: Allow s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on Resource *
Statement 2: Allow s3:PutObject only on arn:aws:s3:::foodquick-ml-training-data/*
Statement 3: Allow ec2:TerminateInstances and ec2:StopInstances, with a Condition checking ec2:ResourceTag/Owner equals ${aws:username}
hints: The EC2 condition uses StringEquals with the key ec2:ResourceTag/Owner
${aws:username} is a policy variable that automatically resolves to the requesting user's name
This Owner-tag condition pattern lets many people share EC2 permissions safely without touching each other's instances

expected_outcome.verifiable_result: A valid 3-statement policy matching all three requirements, with the EC2 statement correctly using the Owner tag condition
expected_outcome.ava_correct: Excellent! இந்த Owner tag condition trick — ரொம்ப powerful pattern. 20 ML engineers இருந்தாலும், ஒவ்வொருத்தரும் தன்ன instances-ஐ மட்டும் control பண்ணுவாங்க, ஒரே policy-ல.
expected_outcome.ava_wrong: கொஞ்சம் பாருங்க — EC2 condition-ல ${aws:username} correct-ஆ use பண்ணீங்களா? இது policy variable, literal string இல்ல. இது தான் ஒவ்வொரு user-க்கும் dynamic-ஆ match ஆகும்.

blocks.block_title: The Policy That Looked Fine But Was AdministratorAccess
blocks.ava_speaks: Security audit-ல flag ஆன ஒரு real policy சொல்றேன்.
blocks.setup: A script written 8 months ago was supposed to 'just read configuration from SSM Parameter Store.' The developer who wrote it has since left the company. Nobody reviewed the policy since it was written.
blocks.what_happened: A routine security audit flagged this as a critical finding — the automated script's policy was found to be functionally identical to AdministratorAccess.
blocks.error_shown: Security scanner alert: 'Policy grants unrestricted access to all AWS actions on all resources. This is equivalent to full administrator access and violates least privilege.'
blocks.the_real_problem: Developer 'quickly' testing something wrote Action: '*' and Resource: '*' — 'இது temporary, later fix பண்றேன்'-ன்னு நினைச்சிருப்பாரு. ஆனா அது 8 மாசம் production-ல அப்படியே இருந்துச்சு. இந்த script compromise ஆனா, attacker-க்கு entire AWS account-ன் full control கிடைச்சிருக்கும்.

fix.result: Script can now ONLY read production parameters — cannot touch any other AWS service or resource

blocks.lesson: Action: '*' Resource: '*' — இது AdministratorAccess-க்கு equal. 'Quick fix, will clean up later' — இது தான் production-ல இருக்க most dangerous policies-க்கான origin story. Never write this, even temporarily.

challenges.question: You need to block ALL delete operations across the entire AWS account during a production freeze, regardless of what individual user policies say. Which IAM feature achieves this?
challenges.answer: AWS Organizations Service Control Policy (SCP). SCP org-level-ல apply ஆகும் — admin கூட override பண்ண முடியாது. Individual user policies-ல Deny போடுறதை விட, SCP ஒரே rule, guaranteed enforcement.

challenges.question: A policy statement has Action: s3:GetObject and Resource: arn:aws:s3:::data-bucket (without the /*). Will this policy successfully allow reading objects?
challenges.answer: இல்ல. GetObject object-level operation, அதுக்கு /* வேணும். இந்த policy technically valid JSON, ஆனா practically எந்த object-ஐயும் read பண்ண முடியாது — ARN format தப்பு.

challenges.question: Why is it better to write TWO statements (one for read, one for write with a condition) instead of ONE complex statement trying to do both?
challenges.answer: Readability and maintainability. Multiple simple statements debug பண்ண easy, audit பண்ண easy. ஒரே statement-ல எல்லாத்தையும் cram பண்ணா, மாசங்களுக்கு அப்புறம் யாருமே அதை புரிஞ்சுக்க மாட்டாங்க.

blocks.ava_speaks: Production-க்கு போற ஒவ்வொரு IAM policy-யும், இந்த review process கடந்து தான் போகும்.

workflow_steps.action: Write the policy targeting the exact minimum permissions needed
workflow_steps.detail: Start narrow. Add permissions only when a real error proves they're needed — never pre-emptively broaden access.

workflow_steps.action: Test using IAM Policy Simulator before attaching to production
workflow_steps.detail: Simulator shows exactly which actions would be Allowed or Denied without actually running them.

workflow_steps.action: Search for wildcards (* in Action or Resource) and justify each one
workflow_steps.detail: Every wildcard in a production policy should have a documented reason. If no one can explain it, remove it.

workflow_steps.action: Peer review — a second engineer reads the policy before it ships
workflow_steps.detail: Fresh eyes catch ARN format mistakes and overly broad permissions that the original author missed.

tools_shown.use: Policy-ஐ attach பண்றத்துக்கு முன்னாடி, அது correct-ஆ work பண்ணுமான்னு test பண்ணலாம்.

tools_shown.tool: AWS Access Analyzer for Policy Validation
tools_shown.use: Policy syntax errors, overly permissive statements automatic-ஆ flag பண்ணும்.

lesson_summary.ava_speaks: இன்னைக்கு real policy design பண்ணீங்க — multiple statements, conditions, precise ARN scoping. Bucket vs object ARN வித்தியாசம், Owner tag condition pattern — இதெல்லாம் இப்போ உங்க toolkit-ல இருக்கு. அடுத்த lesson-ல, least privilege-ஐ ஆழமா பாப்போம் — permissions time-ஓட எப்படி accumulate ஆகுதுன்னும், அதை எப்படி clean பண்றதுன்னும்.

board.title: Lesson C2.2 — Summary
points: ✓ Bucket-level ARN (no /*) for ListBucket, object-level ARN (/*) for GetObject/PutObject
✓ Condition keys restrict access by IP, region, tags, or other request attributes
✓ ${aws:username} policy variable enables per-user dynamic conditions
✓ Action: '*' Resource: '*' is functionally AdministratorAccess — never write this
✓ Multiple clear statements beat one complex statement — always
